title: Corner: Warm Network Outreach Playbook
summary: The complete playbook for landing the first 10 Corner customers through Patrik's personal network. Who to target, what to text, how to follow up, and how to close. The first customer comes from this doc.
content:
Corner: Warm Network Outreach Playbook

For: Patrik Goal: Book 10 discovery calls from your personal network. 10 calls = 5-7 demos = 2-3 closes. Timeline: Week 1 texts go out within 48 hours of S1-S3 Bobby tickets shipping. Read first: corner-discovery-call.md, corner-demo-script.md

The warm network is the only channel that matters right now. Jacob sent 51 cold emails and got zero replies. Your personal network converts at 10x because the trust is pre-built. Every CTA you write, every ad you run, every LinkedIn post -- that all comes AFTER the first 3 customers. Right now, it's just you and your phone.

TARGET PROFILE

Every person on your list should match this profile. If they don't, skip them.

Must-have:

  • Business owner (they make the buying decision)
  • 2-20 employees (big enough to have real ops, small enough to feel the pain personally)
  • Revenue $300k+ (can absorb $3,500/month without it being a crisis)
  • Industry: construction, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, real estate, CPA, marketing agency, chiropractic/dental, law firm
  • Pain point: admin overload, inconsistent follow-up, can't scale without hiring

Strong signal:

  • Phoenix metro (close the loop faster, refer to in-person)
  • Already using ChatGPT and frustrated by the learning curve
  • Has mentioned hiring being expensive or hard to find people
  • Has told Patrik "I need to get more organized"
  • Has seen what AOM does and said some version of "I need that"

Skip for now:

  • Solo operators (one-person shop, no delegation opportunity)
  • B2C retail (wrong use case, too transactional)
  • Government / nonprofit (procurement cycles, committee decisions)
  • Anyone you'd feel uncomfortable texting cold

BUILD THE LIST

Open your contacts. Go through them. Build the list in three tiers.

Tier 1 (5 people): Inner circle These are people who would answer your call right now. You've done business together, you've worked on their project, they trust your judgment without needing a pitch. When you text them, they text back the same day.

Tier 2 (5 people): Warm contacts You know them, they know you. Haven't talked in a while. They'd recognize your name and feel good about hearing from you. Slightly warmer text than Tier 1.

Tier 3 (5 people): Network adjacents Mutual connections. Seen each other at events. You know their name, they know yours. Needs a reminder of context. Lowest conversion rate but worth the shot.

THE OUTREACH SEQUENCE

Day 1: Send Tier 1 (5 texts) Day 3: Send Tier 2 (5 texts) + Day 1 follow-ups if no response Day 7: Send Tier 3 (5 texts) + Day 3 follow-ups if no response

Do not overthink this. Write the names, send the texts. The best time is now.

THE TEXT TEMPLATES

Tier 1 -- Inner Circle

Hey [Name], got 30 seconds?

I built something I think you'd actually find useful. It's an AI operations system for businesses like yours -- basically an entire back-office team that runs 24/7. We've been running AOM on it for the past year.

Worth 30 minutes to show you? No pitch. Just want to see what you think.

What makes this work: Short. No jargon. "No pitch" signals you're not desperate. "What do you think" invites a reaction, not a decision. Under 5 lines so it fits in a text preview without scrolling.

Tier 2 -- Warm Contacts

Hey [Name], been a while.

I've been building something for the past year and we're showing it to a small group of business owners now. It's an AI operations system -- gives you a team of agents that handle follow-up, scheduling, and admin 24/7.

Thought of you because [SPECIFIC REASON -- see examples below].

30-minute demo this week?

Specific reason examples:

  • "you mentioned the admin load was brutal when we talked last year"
  • "I remember you saying you couldn't find good people to hire"
  • "your GC business has the exact workflow this fixes"
  • "you're always trying new tools -- this one's worth seeing"

Make it specific. Generic = spam. Specific = you remembered them.

Tier 3 -- Network Adjacents

Hey [Name] -- Patrik Matheson, we [met at X / connected through Y / worked on Z] a while back.

I'm showing a small group of business owners something I've been building -- an AI operations system that basically gives you a full back-office team running 24/7.

Your [industry] came to mind. Worth a 30-minute look?

Follow-Up Text (Day 3, no response)

Hey [Name] -- following up in case this got buried.

Quick question: is managing your ops and follow-up still a time suck for you? If yes, I think I can help. If no, totally fine.

Just let me know either way.

Why this works: It gives them an easy out. People don't like being chased. When you give them permission to say no, they often don't take it. The response rate on this follow-up is often higher than the first text.

Final Follow-Up (Day 10, still no response)

[Name] -- last one from me on this.

We just opened 3 more spots for the next month. If the timing's off, no worries. If you want to see it before spots fill, just say the word.

After this, move on. Three touches on a warm contact is the max. If they haven't responded, the timing isn't right. Circle back in 60 days.

RESPONSE HANDLING

"Sure, what is it exactly?"

Short version: it's like having a team of 6 AI employees working for your business 24/7. Each specializes -- scheduling, client follow-up, outreach, content, quality control.

You log in and see everything they're doing in real time. It looks like a game but it's your actual operations.

Easier to show than explain. That's why I want the 30 minutes. When works for you?

"Sounds interesting, send me some info"

Happy to. Sending you the overview -- one page, quick read.

But honestly, the info doesn't do it justice. Even if you skim it and decide it's not for you, hop on for 30 minutes. You'll know instantly either way.

[Attach corner-one-pager.pdf]

Send the one-pager AND push for the call. The one-pager alone doesn't close. It's a conversation tool, not a closer.

"Not right now"

Totally fair. When would be a better time -- next month? Q3?

I'd rather set a reminder now than follow up 5 times.

Get a date. Even a loose one. "Next month" is fine -- put a note to text them again on that date.

"How much is it?"

Depends on what you need. We have a starter tier and a growth tier. Growth is $3,500/month -- includes 6 agents, unlimited projects, and a weekly check-in call with me.

For context: a part-time office manager runs $30-40k/year. This is $42k/year but works 24/7, doesn't call in sick, and gets smarter every week.

Let me show you the full thing before you decide. 30 minutes?

"I already use [ChatGPT / Zapier / Monday.com]"

Good -- this isn't a replacement for those. It's what ties them together and runs them for you. ChatGPT answers one question at a time. Corner runs 6 agents in parallel, connected to your actual business data, doing work while you sleep.

Totally different category. Worth seeing in 30 minutes.

POST-DEMO SEQUENCE

Immediately after the demo (same day)

Text:

Great call today. Sending over a summary + pricing -- check your email.

Email: Send the corner-one-pager.pdf (with [BRACKETS] filled in for their business). Subject: "Corner: Your AI team. Next steps."

Day 3 after proposal (no response)

Text:

[Name] -- just following up on the Corner info I sent over. Any questions on the pricing or what's included?

Day 7 after proposal (no response)

Text:

Hey [Name] -- last check-in on Corner. Had a chance to look at the one-pager?

If the pricing works, we can have your office live in 48 hours. If something's holding you back, tell me -- I'd rather fix a real objection than lose a deal to silence.

OBJECTION RESPONSES (close stage)

"It's too expensive."

"Compared to what? A part-time employee is $30-40k/year and doesn't work weekends. Corner is $42k/year and works 24/7. The math usually flips fast when you think about it that way. What would you need to see to feel confident in the ROI?"

"I need to think about it."

"Totally fair. What's the main thing you're thinking through -- is it budget, is it whether the agents can actually do what I showed you, or is it something else?"

Get them to name the real objection. Then address that specifically.

"I'm not sure we're ready for this."

"The businesses that aren't ready are exactly the ones that need this most. Ready means you've already figured out your ops. Ready means you don't need help. Tell me what 'ready' looks like to you."

"Can I see it again?"

"Absolutely. Even better -- let me set you up with a trial office. Your actual projects, your actual team, two agents running for two weeks. No charge. Then you'll know for sure."

This is the pilot. Low-risk entry. Often converts to Growth tier after the trial.

SUCCESS METRICS

Metric Target
Texts sent (Week 1) 15
Response rate 50%+ (warm network)
Discovery calls booked 8+
Demos completed 6+
Proposals sent 5+
Closes 2-3 (first 30 days)

Reality check: If you send 15 texts and get 3 responses, the text templates need work. If you get 8 responses and book 2 discovery calls, the booking language needs work. If you do 6 demos and send 0 proposals, the demo needs work. Track each stage so you know where the funnel breaks.

TIMING

Do not send texts until S1-S3 Bobby tickets are shipped:

  • S1: sessionStorage auth bypass removed
  • S2: /onboarding vercel.json route fixed
  • S3: DEFAULT_PROJECTS hardcode replaced with per-client Supabase

If a prospect clicks around after the demo and hits a DevTools bypass or sees "KOHRS" in their task list, the deal dies. These three tickets protect every deal you run.

The moment S1-S3 ship: send the first 5 texts.
